read.sections.0.text.source:
A history painting presents an account of the past through figures, setting and arrangement. Its artist chooses which moment to show and whose actions seem important. Two paintings of Prince Diponegoro's capture show how such choices can support power. They can also challenge its public image. The pictures also have histories of their own. Later audiences can give them meanings that their first viewers would not have shared.

Diponegoro was a Javanese prince and a major leader of resistance during the Java War of 1825–1830. Dutch colonial authorities sought to control Java, where local rulers and communities had their own interests. Colonial rule means control of a territory by an outside power. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro was arrested at Magelang during talks. He had been given a promise of safe conduct: a promise that he could come and go safely. The arrest helped bring the war to an end. It happened in the Dutch East Indies, long before Indonesia proclaimed its independence in 1945.
read.sections.0.text.back:
A history painting presents an account of the past through figures, setting and arrangement. Its artist chooses which moment to show and whose actions look important. Two paintings of the arrest of Prince Diponegoro show how such choices can support power. Those choices can also challenge the public image of that power. These pictures also have their own histories. Later viewers can give them meanings that their first viewers did not share.

Diponegoro was a Javanese prince and a main leader of resistance during the Java War of 1825–1830. The Dutch colonial authorities tried to take control of Java, where local rulers and communities had their own interests. Colonial rule means control of a territory by a power from outside. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro was arrested at Magelang during talks. He had been given a promise of safe conduct, that is, a promise that he could come and go safely. The arrest helped end the war. This happened in the Dutch East Indies, long before Indonesia proclaimed its independence in 1945.
read.sections.0.text.note: "Prince" is "Putera" in the readings; Malaysian writing often keeps the Javanese title "Pangeran Diponegoro". Reviewer to choose. "proclaimed" is "mengisytiharkan", not the Indonesian "proklamasi" (Southeast Asia's TERMS).

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
A history painting tells a story about the past. The artist picks one moment and who looks important. Two paintings show the capture of Prince Diponegoro. Art can back up power or question it. Later, people gave the paintings new meanings.

Diponegoro was a prince from Java. He led a fight against Dutch control in the Java War, from 1825 to 1830. Colonial rule means rule of a land by an outside power. Dutch officials wanted to rule Java. But the rulers and people of Java had their own goals. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro came to Magelang for talks. The Dutch had promised he would be safe. But they arrested him. This helped end the war. Then, the land was called the Dutch East Indies. Indonesia became free much later, in 1945.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
A history painting tells a story about the past. The artist chooses one moment and who looks important. Two paintings show the arrest of Prince Diponegoro. Art can support power or question it. Later, people gave new meanings to the paintings.

Diponegoro was a prince from Java. He led a fight against Dutch control in the Java War, from 1825 to 1830. Colonial rule means rule of a land by an outside power. Dutch officials wanted to rule Java. But the rulers and people of Java had their own goals. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro came to Magelang for talks. The Dutch had promised he would be safe. But they arrested him. This helped end the war. At that time, the land was called the Dutch East Indies. Indonesia became independent much later, in 1945.

read.sections.1.text.source:
The Dutch artist Nicolaas Pieneman painted his version around 1830–1835. It was a commission for General Hendrik Merkus de Kock. He was the officer who ordered the arrest. Its familiar title, The Submission of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock, encourages viewers to see the scene as a surrender. Upright Dutch officers, the raised Dutch flag and followers gathered below make colonial authority look certain. The commission matters: this was an account made for the victorious commander.

Raden Saleh completed The Arrest of Prince Diponegoro in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He built his painting career through training and patronage in Europe. He worked across connected but unequal worlds. Both praise in Europe and his ties to his homeland shaped his career. His life does not fit a simple split between a European way of painting and a separate Javanese view. Oil painting could carry an account that questioned colonial power.
read.sections.1.text.back:
The Dutch artist Nicolaas Pieneman painted his version around 1830–1835. The painting was a commission for General Hendrik Merkus de Kock. He was the officer who ordered the arrest. Its familiar title, The Submission of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock, encourages viewers to see the scene as a surrender. Dutch officers standing upright, the raised Dutch flag and the followers gathered below make colonial power look certain. The commission matters: this is an account made for the victorious commander.

Raden Saleh completed The Arrest of Prince Diponegoro in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He built his career as a painter through training and patronage in Europe. He worked across worlds that were connected but unequal. Praise in Europe and his ties with his homeland both shaped his career. His life does not fit a simple split between a European way of painting and a separate Javanese view. Oil painting could carry an account that questioned colonial power.

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
A Dutch artist, Nicolaas Pieneman, painted his version in about 1830 to 1835. It was a commission from General De Kock. He ordered the arrest. A commission is a request to make a work. The title calls the scene a submission. That means giving up. Dutch officers stand tall. A Dutch flag flies high. His followers are lower down. So Dutch power looks sure and strong. The painting was made for the winner.

Raden Saleh finished his painting in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He trained in Europe, and people there paid for his art. He lived between two worlds that were not equal. He won praise in Europe, but he felt close to his home. So we cannot just call his art Dutch or Javanese. His oil painting could question Dutch power.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
A Dutch artist, Nicolaas Pieneman, painted his version around 1830 to 1835. The painting was a commission from General De Kock. He was the one who ordered the arrest. A commission is a request to make a work. Its title calls the scene a submission. That means admitting defeat. Dutch officers stand upright. A Dutch flag flies high. Diponegoro's followers are below. So Dutch power looks certain and strong. The painting was made for the side that won.

Raden Saleh finished his painting in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He studied in Europe, and people there paid for his art. He lived between two worlds that were not equal. He was praised in Europe, but he felt close to his homeland. So we cannot call his art only Dutch or Javanese. His oil painting could question Dutch power.

read.sections.2.text.source:
In Saleh's composition, Diponegoro stands upright near De Kock, surrounded by distressed followers. His white clothing and firm posture give him dignity at the moment of capture. The crowd brings the emotional cost of the arrest into the foreground. Unlike Pieneman, Saleh includes no flying Dutch flag. These differences help explain why scholars see the later painting as a challenge to the earlier one. That reading connects visible choices with historical context. A painted face alone cannot prove what a person actually felt.

The painting's later life matters too. The Dutch government returned Saleh's work to Indonesia in 1978. Diponegoro's image has appeared on posters, monuments and other artworks. It has helped later generations debate heroism, resistance and national identity. National identity means the ideas and memories through which people feel they belong to a nation. Such uses belong to Indonesia's changing history. They do not prove that Saleh held every later nationalist belief. Neither painting speaks for every Dutch or Javanese person. Neither gives a complete, neutral history of the war. Together, they show how art takes part in struggles over whose account becomes public memory.
read.sections.2.text.back:
In Saleh's composition, Diponegoro stands upright near De Kock, surrounded by grieving followers. His white clothing and firm posture give him dignity at the moment he is arrested. The crowd brings the emotional cost of the arrest into the front part. Unlike Pieneman, Saleh does not include a flying Dutch flag. These differences help explain why scholars see the later painting as a challenge to the earlier painting. That reading connects visible choices with historical context. A painted face alone cannot prove what a person really felt.

The painting's later life also matters. The Dutch government returned Saleh's work to Indonesia in 1978. Diponegoro's image has appeared on posters, monuments and other artworks. The image has helped later generations debate heroism, resistance and national identity. National identity means the ideas and memories that make people feel they are part of a nation. Uses like these belong to Indonesia's changing history. These uses do not prove that Saleh held every nationalist belief that came later. Neither painting speaks for every Dutch or Javanese person. Neither gives a complete and neutral history of the war. Together, these paintings show how art takes part in struggles over whose account becomes public memory.
read.sections.2.text.note: "distressed" is "bersedih" (grieving, sad); "dalam kesusahan" is the alternative.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Saleh's composition is different. A composition is how the parts of a picture are arranged. The prince stands tall near De Kock. He wears white. The men and women around him are upset. This gives him dignity, even as he is caught. The crowd shows how painful the arrest was. Saleh's painting has no Dutch flag. So experts say it pushes back against Pieneman's story. But a painted face cannot prove what a real person felt.

Later, in 1978, the Dutch government gave it back to Indonesia. The prince's picture has been on posters and statues. People use it to talk about heroes and the fight for freedom. They also talk about national identity. That means the ideas that make people feel part of a nation. This does not prove what Saleh believed. Neither painting speaks for all Dutch or all Javanese people. Neither tells the whole story of the war. People still argue about whose story is remembered.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:
Saleh's composition is different. A composition is the way the parts of a picture are arranged. The prince stands upright near De Kock. He is dressed in white. The men and women around him are grieving. This gives him dignity, even though he is arrested. The crowd shows how painful the arrest was. Saleh's painting has no Dutch flag. So experts say this painting pushes back against Pieneman's story. But a painted face cannot prove what a real person felt.

Later, in 1978, the Dutch government returned it to Indonesia. The prince's picture is on posters and statues. People use it to talk about heroes and the struggle for freedom. They also talk about national identity. That means the ideas that make people feel part of a nation. This does not prove what Saleh believed. Neither painting speaks for all Dutch people or all Javanese people. Neither tells the whole story of the war. People still debate whose story is remembered.

write.prompt.source: In two or three sentences, explain how one difference between these paintings changes the story of the arrest. Say who a painting was made by or for.
write.prompt.back: In two or three sentences, explain how one difference between these paintings changes the story of the arrest. State by whom or for whom a painting was made.

write.example.source: In Pieneman's painting, Dutch officers stand tall under a Dutch flag. The prince's followers are lower down. Pieneman painted it for General De Kock, who ordered the arrest. So the scene looks like a surrender. In Saleh's painting, there is no Dutch flag, and the prince stands tall in white. This matters because it gives him dignity. It also shows the arrest as a painful moment for his followers.
write.example.back: In Pieneman's painting, Dutch officers stand upright under a Dutch flag. The prince's followers are below. Pieneman painted it for General De Kock, who ordered the arrest. So the scene looks like a surrender. In Saleh's painting, there is no Dutch flag, and the prince stands upright in white clothes. This matters because the painting gives him dignity. The painting also shows the arrest as a painful moment for his followers.

visual.alt.source: Oil painting. Prince Diponegoro, in white, stands at the top of the steps of a veranda on the same level as Dutch officers, one of whom gestures toward a waiting carriage. His followers crowd the steps and ground below, some kneeling and one woman clinging to him, with mountains in the distance.
visual.alt.back: Oil painting. Prince Diponegoro, dressed in white, stands at the top of the steps of a veranda on the same level as Dutch officers, and one of the officers points towards a waiting carriage. His followers crowd the steps and the ground below, some kneeling and a woman clinging to him, with mountains in the distance.
visual.alt.note: "carriage" is "kereta kuda" (horse-drawn carriage), because "kereta" alone is a car.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: Colonial conquest and war: teach colonial rule as an unequal relationship of power. Keep the arrest and the war non-graphic, with no reenactment or role-play. Keep the documented breach of safe conduct (Diponegoro was arrested during negotiations despite a promise of safe conduct) apart from interpretations of poses and faces. Don't describe the Java War as a conflict between two modern nation-states: in 1830 Java was part of the Dutch East Indies, and Indonesia proclaimed independence in 1945.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: Colonial conquest and war: teach colonial rule as an unequal relationship of power. Tell the arrest and the war without gruesome detail, without re-enactment or role-play. Keep the documented breach of safe conduct (Diponegoro was arrested during negotiations although he had been promised safe conduct) apart from interpretations of poses and faces. Don't describe the Java War as a conflict between two modern nation-states: in 1830 Java was part of the Dutch East Indies, and Indonesia proclaimed independence in 1945.

sensitiveNotes.1.source: Identity and belief: Diponegoro was also an Islamic religious leader. No learner is asked to speak for his faith or community, to share their own religion, identity or family, or to represent Indonesians, Javanese or Dutch people. For many learners in Indonesia, Diponegoro is a national hero; treat that later memory as real history to learn about, while keeping it apart from what the 1830 sources show. Accept reasoned answers about either painting without requiring a feeling about it.

Accept reasoned answers about either painting without requiring a feeling about it.
sensitiveNotes.1.note: The English says "learners in Indonesia"; kept, although the Malay version is for a partner in Malaysia, where many learners may also know of Diponegoro.

educatorNotes.2.source: Sources: the Rijksmuseum record gives Pieneman's commission, the safe conduct, the current title and the date range c. 1830–c. 1835 (some older records say 1835). Elly Kent's article (National Gallery Singapore) supports the missing flag, the scholars' reading and the later uses. The Cabinet Secretariat page supports the capture place and date, the 1857 date and the 1978 return; the lesson does not adopt its claims that particular colours prove one intention, or its incorrect claim that Islam forbids all fighting during Ramadan, and its photographs are not used. The 1945 proclamation is from the State Secretariat (setneg.go.id).

educatorNotes.3.source: Images: both are Wikimedia Commons' faithful reproductions of two-dimensional public-domain paintings (Saleh died in 1880, Pieneman in 1860), so the credit links the exact Commons file pages, where the rights statements are. Indonesian sources place Saleh's painting at the Yogyakarta Presidential Palace and at Istana Negara, Jakarta: one work, so the caption gives no fixed display place. Commons reports a heritage registration, RNCB.20190219.01.001562, which is not a museum accession number. Don't swap in the separate "Rijksmuseum Official" Commons file of Pieneman's painting, which carries a CC BY 3.0 statement.
